home.heroSub: An in-depth article series on the First Nations and Inuit who have lived on Quebec territory for millennia.
home.introTitle: A history that begins long before Quebec
home.introP1: Long before Jacques Cartier reached the St. Lawrence in 1534, dozens of Indigenous nations had lived on this territory for millennia. Hunters, farmers, navigators, diplomats — each people developed a unique civilization, rooted in the land and passed down through extraordinarily rich oral traditions.
home.introP2: This series invites you to discover the 11 First Nations and the Inuit of Nunavik — their history, culture, traditions and place in Quebec today. An invitation to respect and understanding.
home.nationsSub: Click a nation to read its article
home.serieSub: 8 series of ten articles (#1 to #80): spirituality, history, Quebec know-how, forgotten wisdom, living culture… Each card opens the full article.
home.serieNotice: All articles in one place. Series 1 (#1–#10) to Series 8 (#71–#80) — listen button (▶ Listen) on each page.
home.communityP: Share these articles, discuss, and learn more about Indigenous peoples in Quebec.

carnetsPage.metaTitle: Pierre le Fouineur's Notebooks — First Nations of Quebec
carnetsPage.title: 📜 Pierre le Fouineur's Notebooks
carnetsPage.intro: Stories left by my friend Pierre's great-grandfather — coureur des bois, trade with First Nations, a treasury of knowledge about Quebec's eleven nations. I pass them on as written, inventing nothing.
carnetsPage.portrait: Pierre le Fouineur — coureur des bois in Quebec. He walked the portages, listened to the Elders, wrote at night in leather notebooks. Each notebook explores one skill: hunting, fishing, fire, winter, portages… An old text, shared with respect.
carnetsPage.seeAllArticles: See all 80 articles in the series →
carnetsPage.card76desc: Bows, canoes, traps, sacred tobacco — eleven nations, eleven philosophies of the hunt.
carnetsPage.card77desc: Harpoons, traps, tobacco protocols — respect for fish and water.
carnetsPage.card78desc: Friction, sacred circle, fire prayer — a liturgy of the Elders.
carnetsPage.card79desc: Snow, tracks, sleds and winter fire — a report in 4 parts (one every 2 days).
carnetsPage.card80desc: Diaries 1892-1921: travel by water and land, with dates and landmarks along the route.
